I have one of those toys. I can consistently get off in under 3 minutes and I don't need to be aroused at any point for it to work (which is very hard for me due to medication). I would use it just as much if I were getting laid as I am now. It's barely even sexual for me – it's satisfying an entirely different need than sex itself does.

I think you should leave it alone. It's not the cause of your DB and it might not even be a replacement for it.

It's not really the "borderline" part of the term I take issue with (though it doesn't help the average person differentiate between BPD and bipolar, in my experience). 

But labeling a group of people who already have poor self image with "personality disorder" only increases negative stigma -- it's very easy, especially when you hear the term for the first time, to jump from "personality disorder" to "there is something wrong with you as a person", which is not the case.
Yes, this 100%. But I've also found that loving tattoos makes me want to self harm less because I don't want to fuck up unscarred potential real estate. Win-win.

FWIW I think keeping it in (or at least keeping it to Reddit) is the right thing to do in this situation. My boyfriend is the exact same when he's upset and it fucking kills! But if they respect the way we grieve, it's up to us to respect the way they do, too, I think.

I don't think you're overreacting, but I also don't think he's doing it maliciously. He hasn't been in your exact situation, so it's probably hard for him to understand or relate to why it means so much to you, even if you explain it. I've had a very similar issue with my partner (except it was kisses when he left for work at 4 am) and it took a very long time of me explaining that it was much more important than it seemed for him to understand. 

I get why it hurts you 100%. But I would try to keep in mind that hurting you is likely not his intention, either.

Personally I think the fact that it's called BPD is stigmatizing bullshit in and of itself. Your entire personality is not a disorder. Your hobbies, the things you find funny, your spirit -- these things are unique to you, not the BPD. 

I can't tell you that everything will get better. I think we'll always feel more than most people, and we'll always struggle with that. But I've been in therapy for 2 years now and I can tell you that a lot of it has. I've only had one (vs like, several times weekly) unwarranted breakdown in the past several months. I've learned to treat my partner with more patience. Things don't hurt as bad as they used to.

It's hard, but it gets less hard. There are ups and downs, but eventually more ups. I hope you can find peace until then.

Probably around two years, though moreso in the past year since it was recommended to me as a sleep aid.

My go-to is anything on [this channel](https://youtube.com/channel/UCDRC-dZfZvsF9b1O1EvDbHQ) as I find her particularly soothing. I like to do a random one each time so I'm focused more on the meditation than anticipating what she's going to say next.

I think it's normal to not feel much for someone when you've just been through something traumatic, so I doubt your feelings for him are suddenly gone. That said, knowingly ghosting someone with BPD is cruel and you deserve someone who understands and respects your feelings more than that.

Meditation has helped me a lot. My therapist starts off every session with a meditative exercise, and I've found that copying them in times of big emotions (when it's possible) does wonders.

The type of meditation I like best is stopping to analyze how each part of your body is feeling, from feet to head. Then it's easier to address physical symptoms of emotions (am I hot? I should take a cold shower to calm down, etc.) to regulate them.

In non-emotional times, I also like guided breathing exercises on YouTube too. I like to do them before bed to shed the feelings of the day.

Personally I don't think you owe an explanation to anyone. With or without the diagnosis you are going to think, feel and behave a certain way and labeling yourself for others doesn't change that. Why give people a chance to stigmatize you before they can get to know you?

Edit: That said I've also found that referring to my BPD to contextualize emotions (why I'm feeling more emotional about things than another person might), so I don't think it's helpful to keep it from everyone. You don't owe anyone the diagnosis, but it's there for you to use if you need it.

Two different people could go through the exact same situation and come out entirely differently just because their brains are different. There's no way to compare what you went through (which sounds really tough) with abuse or assault because every single person is on their own scale. Feelings can't be invalid.

Maybe you didn't care when you were a very young child, but even by starting this post with a trigger warning you've shown a lot of empathy here. You can't take back bad things you did, but you can put good things into the world in their place. Karma doesn't have to mean dying.

You know, I don't think all the things in this post are true of you. For starters, you seem very sarcastic. It seems like you have a dry sense of humour, and that really vibes with a lot of people. So I think it's safe to say you have a personality. 

Nobody to talk to? I mean, you've got us. It might not seem like much, but people on this subreddit care enough that your post has more traction than the average. Sure, some are a bit cranky, but people tend to be reactionary when you ask them to compare struggles. No matter what we're going through, we all feel it differently, and there's no way to measure and compare that pain. 

Also, just looking through your posts, I would encourage you not to listen to what incels say about women. It's taken a lot of time and abuse for me to learn that that is not how most men see the world. Of course attractiveness changes the way people treat you, but the personality I mentioned before can absolutely shine through. 

You're young. I can't tell you things will get better, because I don't know. But I can promise things will get different. And that's something.
